feat(wire): closing overlap, centre-line slit and open-run skims for Wire Contour

Wire Contour gains a closing overlap (#3216): the ride continues past
the seam by the stated arc length before the lead-out back to the
threading point, so the start of the cut is burnt over and no witness
mark is left. A skim inherits it. It is refused by name where there is
no seam to close past - with tabs (tabs pin the seam) and on an open
run - and a negative length is refused at the door.

The new Centre side cuts an open run as a centre-line slit: the wire
rides the run itself, the kerf burns both sides, no side is kept, and
the kerf law has no product to protect (said on the report line, never
silent). Open runs now take skim passes too: each re-enters from the
air at the run's start end and is walked in the run's own direction; a
reversed pass is refused by name.

The project file reads the new fields with serde defaults, so every
file written before this reads unchanged. The wire page offers the
overlap row and the centre side, and the verify judges a centre slit
as an open run whose ends' clearance is still checked.

Fixes #3216

fix(wire): the closing overlap rework after the PR #3617 safety review

- the Centre slit's run-out clearance joins the generation stamp, so an
  edited or re-stated clearance reads Stale, never Ok with the old path
  (cutting.rs; wire_stamp pins the edit and the project reload);
- the overlap's ride includes the seam edge's own remainder back to the
  seam, so a stated overlap covers exactly its arc in both directions,
  and a ride longer than one full lap is refused by name (ring.rs);
- an open run's skim passes are rethreaded in the air: a travel move (a
  rapid, no wire through it) marks each pass boundary, the wire laws
  judge each pass at its own kerf and its own ends (sim verify splits at
  the boundaries), the post announces each skim after the travel, and
  wire-iso.cps cuts the wire, travels and threads anew around it (new
  wire_contour_open_skims golden; the Sodick post keeps refusing the
  structure by name at its rapid guard);
- a stated overlap beside a no-core burnout, a 4-axis cut or a constant
  taper is refused by name at the command door (wire_op::overlap_refusal
  through condition_of), never generated with the overlap silently
  dropped and never handed to the taper builder as an unclean ring;
- the merge with origin/main completed: main's new arc modules take the
  Centre side in their closed-profile refusals, and the arc tests state
  the overlap field.
